verdicts.evidence: The mutated branch is genuinely taken, and I measured it being taken: on a mission carrying a row with status `todo` (which `parseManifest` keeps and the guard normally skips) the output is still byte-identical. `c[<unknown status>]++` writes `NaN` under a NEW key - after the mutated branch runs, `c` is `{"applied":1,"deviated":0,"n/a":0,"todo":NaN}` - and the NIST draft, the only consumer of `confCounts`, reads only `c.applied`, `c.deviated` and `c["n/a"]`, which are untouched. Sensitivity control: the two diverge the moment a renderer enumerates the object instead of naming the three keys (`Object.entries(c)` would print `todo: NaN`), and no renderer does.

verdicts.evidence: Measured on 17 missions. On the shipped reference mission the NIST AI RMF draft's MEASURE/TEVV line goes from "From your mission: **23 applied - 0 deviated - 13 n/a** across 36 rule(s)" to "**0 applied - 0 deviated - 0 n/a** across 36 rule(s)". The sentence introduces those figures as what "Feeds MEASURE 2.x - documented, repeatable test methodology and results", so a reader takes them as the count of controls carrying evidence: 36 rules accounted for, none of them applied. The document is emitted at exit 0 with the true gate verdict beside it, which makes the two halves of the same pack contradict each other. `confCounts` feeds ONLY `renderNistAiRmf` - the ISO draft keeps its own inline copy of the same loop - and the single golden fixture renders eu-ai-act, so nothing in the net visits this line.

verdicts.evidence: The complement of the same guard: only statuses that are NOT among the three are counted, so `applied`, `deviated` and `n/a` never increment. Measured on 17 missions, with the identical rendered result as the `-> false` sibling: "**0 applied - 0 deviated - 0 n/a** across 36 rule(s)" in the NIST AI RMF draft's MEASURE/TEVV section on a mission with 23 applied and 13 n/a rows. Same recipe, same reason nothing noticed.

verdicts.evidence: Measured on 17 missions: the NIST AI RMF draft's MEASURE/TEVV line reads "**-23 applied - 0 deviated - -13 n/a** across 36 rule(s)" on the shipped reference mission. Negative counts read as absurd to a human, but the document is still written at exit 0, nothing in the pipeline refuses it, and the OSCAL schema check does not cover the markdown drafts. A regulated reader who takes the number rather than the sign gets a control-implementation count that is wrong in both magnitude and meaning.
